passages.text: You therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy, his spiritual child.
Paul calls Timothy "my child."
Paul tells Timothy to be strong.
Paul says this strength comes from grace.
This grace is found in Christ Jesus.
passages.original: Σὺ οὖν τέκνον μου ἐνδυναμοῦ ἐν τῇ χάριτι τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: And the things that you have heard me say among many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be qualified to teach others as well.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy, his spiritual child.
Paul has taught Timothy many things.
Many witnesses heard Paul teach these things.
Paul tells Timothy to entrust these teachings to faithful men.
These faithful men must be able to teach others also.
passages.original: καὶ ἃ ἤκουσας παρ’ ἐμοῦ διὰ πολλῶν μαρτύρων ταῦτα παράθου πιστοῖς ἀνθρώποις οἵτινες ἱκανοὶ ἔσονται καὶ ἑτέρους διδάξαι

passages.text: Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy, his spiritual child.
Paul calls Timothy to join him in suffering.
Paul tells Timothy to suffer as a good soldier.
Paul says the soldier serves Christ Jesus.
passages.original: Συνκακοπάθησον ὡς καλὸς στρατιώτης Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: A soldier refrains from entangling himself in civilian affairs, in order to please the one who enlisted him.
passages.sermon:
A soldier serves in the army.
He does not get involved in everyday business.
He avoids civilian affairs.
He does this to please the person who enlisted him.
passages.original: οὐδεὶς στρατευόμενος ἐμπλέκεται ταῖς τοῦ βίου πραγματείαις ἵνα τῷ στρατολογήσαντι ἀρέσῃ

passages.text: Likewise, a competitor does not receive the crown unless he competes according to the rules.
passages.sermon:
A competitor enters a contest.
He wants to win a crown.
He must follow the rules to win.
If he does not follow the rules, he does not receive the crown.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ἀθλῇ τις οὐ στεφανοῦται ἐὰν μὴ νομίμως ἀθλήσῃ

passages.text: The hardworking farmer should be the first to partake of the crops.
passages.sermon: A farmer works hard.\r\nHe should receive a share of the crops first.\r\nHe deserves to benefit from his labor before others.
passages.original: τὸν κοπιῶντα γεωργὸν δεῖ πρῶτον τῶν καρπῶν μεταλαμβάνειν

passages.text: Consider what I am saying, for the Lord will give you insight into all things.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy.
Paul tells Timothy to think about his words.
Paul says, "Consider what I am saying."
The Lord will give you understanding.
The Lord gives insight in everything.
passages.original: νόει ὃ λέγω δώσει γάρ σοι ὁ Κύριος σύνεσιν ἐν πᾶσιν

passages.text: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, as proclaimed by my gospel, for which I suffer to the extent of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God cannot be chained!
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is the Son of David.
Jesus Christ rose from the dead.
My gospel proclaims Jesus Christ.
I suffer because of this gospel.
I am chained like a criminal.
But God’s word is not chained.
passages.original: Μνημόνευε Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐγηγερμένον ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυίδ κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου ἐν ᾧ κακοπαθῶ μέχρι δεσμῶν ὡς κακοῦργος ἀλλὰ ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐ δέδεται

passages.text: For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul suffers many things.
Paul endures all things.
Paul does this for the sake of God’s chosen people.
Paul wants the elect to receive salvation.
This salvation is found in Christ Jesus.
This salvation comes with eternal glory.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο πάντα ὑπομένω διὰ τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ σωτηρίας τύχωσιν τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ μετὰ δόξης αἰωνίου

passages.text: This is a trustworthy saying: If we died with Him, we will also live with Him; if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He will also deny us; if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.
passages.sermon:
This saying is trustworthy.
If we died with Jesus, we will also live with Him.
If we endure, we will also reign with Him.
If we deny Him, He will also deny us.
If we are faithless, He remains faithful.
He cannot deny Himself.
passages.original: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος Εἰ γὰρ συναπεθάνομεν καὶ συζήσομεν εἰ ὑπομένομεν καὶ συμβασιλεύσομεν εἰ ἀρνησόμεθα κἀκεῖνος ἀρνήσεται ἡμᾶς εἰ ἀπιστοῦμεν ἐκεῖνος πιστὸς μένει ἀρνήσασθαι γὰρ ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται

passages.text: Remind the believers of these things, charging them before God to avoid quarreling over words, which succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy.
Paul is a leader in the early church.
Paul gives Timothy instructions for the church.
Paul tells Timothy to remind the believers of important truths.
Paul commands Timothy to do this before God.
Paul tells Timothy to warn the believers.
Paul tells them not to quarrel about words.
Quarreling about words is not useful.
Quarreling about words only harms those who listen.
Quarreling leads the listeners to ruin.
passages.original: Ταῦτα ὑπομίμνῃσκε διαμαρτυρόμενος ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ μὴ λογομαχεῖν ἐπ’ οὐδὲν χρήσιμον ἐπὶ καταστροφῇ τῶν ἀκουόντων

passages.text: Make every effort to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy.
Paul urges Timothy to serve God faithfully.
Paul tells Timothy to work hard.
Timothy must try to please God.
Timothy must show himself as approved by God.
Timothy must be a worker who is not ashamed.
Timothy must handle the word of truth correctly.
passages.original: Σπούδασον σεαυτὸν δόκιμον παραστῆσαι τῷ Θεῷ ἐργάτην ἀνεπαίσχυντον ὀρθοτομοῦντα τὸν λόγον τῆς ἀληθείας

passages.text: But avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which will only lead to more ungodliness, and the talk of such men will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus, who have deviated from the truth. They say that the resurrection has already occurred, and they undermine the faith of some.
passages.sermon:
Avoid irreverent and empty talk.
This kind of talk only leads to more ungodliness.
The words of such people will spread like gangrene.
Hymenaeus and Philetus are examples of these people.
They have missed the truth.
They say the resurrection has already happened.
They destroy the faith of some people.
passages.original: Τὰς δὲ βεβήλους κενοφωνίας περιΐστασο ἐπὶ πλεῖον γὰρ προκόψουσιν ἀσεβείας καὶ ὁ λόγος αὐτῶν ὡς γάγγραινα νομὴν ἕξει ὧν ἐστιν Ὑμέναιος καὶ Φιλητός οἵτινες περὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἠστόχησαν λέγοντες τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἤδη γεγονέναι καὶ ἀνατρέπουσιν τήν τινων πίστιν

passages.text: Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.”
passages.sermon:
God’s foundation is strong.
God’s foundation stands firm.
This foundation has a seal.
The seal says, “The Lord knows those who belong to Him.”
The seal also says, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from wrongdoing.”
passages.original: Ὁ μέντοι στερεὸς θεμέλιος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἕστηκεν ἔχων τὴν σφραγῖδα ταύτην Ἔγνω Κύριος τοὺς ὄντας αὐτοῦ καί Ἀποστήτω ἀπὸ ἀδικίας πᾶς ὁ ὀνομάζων τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου

passages.text: A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.
passages.sermon:
A large house has many kinds of vessels.
Some vessels are made of gold.
Some vessels are made of silver.
Some vessels are made of wood.
Some vessels are made of clay.
People use some vessels for honor.
People use other vessels for common purposes.
passages.original: Ἐν μεγάλῃ δὲ οἰκίᾳ οὐκ ἔστιν μόνον σκεύη χρυσᾶ καὶ ἀργυρᾶ ἀλλὰ καὶ ξύλινα καὶ ὀστράκινα καὶ ἃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν ἃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν

passages.text: So if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified, useful to the Master, and prepared for every good work.
passages.sermon:
God is the Master.
A person can cleanse himself from what is unfit.
If a person does this, he becomes a vessel for honor.
He becomes sanctified.
He becomes useful to the Master.
He becomes prepared for every good work.
passages.original: ἐὰν οὖν τις ἐκκαθάρῃ ἑαυτὸν ἀπὸ τούτων ἔσται σκεῦος εἰς τιμήν ἡγιασμένον εὔχρηστον τῷ δεσπότῃ εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἡτοιμασμένον

passages.text: Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Timothy.
Paul gives instructions for Christian living.
Paul says, "Flee from youthful passions."
Do not follow desires that come from immaturity.
Pursue righteousness.
Pursue faith.
Pursue love.
Pursue peace.
Join with others who call on the Lord.
These people call on the Lord from a pure heart.
passages.original: Τὰς δὲ νεωτερικὰς ἐπιθυμίας φεῦγε δίωκε δὲ δικαιοσύνην πίστιν ἀγάπην εἰρήνην μετὰ τῶν ἐπικαλουμένων τὸν Κύριον ἐκ καθαρᾶς καρδίας

passages.text: But reject foolish and ignorant speculation, for you know that it breeds quarreling.
passages.sermon:
Reject foolish questions.
Reject ignorant questions.
You know these questions cause arguments.
These questions lead to quarreling.
passages.original: Τὰς δὲ μωρὰς καὶ ἀπαιδεύτους ζητήσεις παραιτοῦ εἰδὼς ὅτι γεννῶσιν μάχας

passages.text: And a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing.
passages.sermon:
A servant of the Lord must not fight.
A servant of the Lord must not argue.
A servant of the Lord must be kind to everyone.
A servant of the Lord must be able to teach.
A servant of the Lord must be patient with others.
passages.original: δοῦλον δὲ Κυρίου οὐ δεῖ μάχεσθαι ἀλλὰ ἤπιον εἶναι πρὸς πάντας διδακτικόν ἀνεξίκακον

passages.text: He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth.
passages.sermon:
A servant of the Lord must teach gently.
He must correct those who oppose him.
He must do this with kindness.
He hopes that God will give them repentance.
He hopes God will lead them to know the truth.
passages.original: ἐν πραΰτητι παιδεύοντα τοὺς ἀντιδιατιθεμένους μή‿ ποτε δώῃ αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς μετάνοιαν εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας

passages.text: Then they will come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will.
passages.sermon:
Some people are trapped by the devil.
The devil has taken them captive.
They do what the devil wants.
They will come to their senses.
They will escape from the devil’s trap.
passages.original: καὶ ἀνανήψωσιν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ διαβόλου παγίδος ἐζωγρημένοι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ ἐκείνου θέλημα
